purpose: Fix the mechanical findings from the 2026-08-23 stress-test drive (scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md). Fifteen corrections across the Hub API, the scheduler and the dashboard, each with a regression test. The two architectural changes from that drive - 2026-08-23-a-reviewer-can-see-the-work and 2026-08-23-the-hop-budget-is-a-real-bound - are specified and validated but deliberately NOT in this queue; they are for an attended session with the operator, who is awake from 08:00.

queue.title: Backend papercuts, no UI files
queue.detail: Six independent corrections, all Python, each with its own regression test. (F4) hub/hub/api/v1/projects.py: on POST /projects/open of a git repository, adopt the branch that GET /projects/{id}/main-branch-suggestion already computes, instead of leaving main_branch null. Integration silently skips without it. (F8) hub/hub/requirement_evidence.py: the refusal for an unknown evidence decision must name the permitted values ('accepted', 'rejected') the way model_catalog's permission_mode refusal names its four, and the route must return 422 not 403. A malformed enum is a validation error, and an agent reading the status code concludes it lacks permission and stops retrying. (F7) Same module: refuse or flag a second piece of evidence for the same requirement, task and commit. Note the existing `digest` column is NOT a duplicate detector; it pins the requirement's wording at production time. (F16) hub/hub/api/v1/tasks.py: TaskResponse must echo loop_id. POST /tasks accepts it and returns null, so a caller cannot confirm the task joined the loop. (S2) hub/hub/utils.py: widen short_id() from 8 hex characters to 12. Columns are already String(64) so NO migration is needed and existing ids keep working; this moves the birthday bound from ~77k rows to ~800M on event_logs and agent_outputs, the two tables nothing prunes. (F6/F18) hub/hub/run_task_binding.py: bind_run_to_task must set task.assignee the way the loop's claim already does at scheduler.py:979. Today a task moved to in_progress by a direct trigger shows no assignee and reports assignee_status 'idle' about a running agent.

queue.title: Scheduler honesty: F11, F13, and the cron refusal
queue.detail: (F11) hub/hub/scheduler.py: _do_fire_job increments job.run_count and stamps job.last_run at lines ~796-797, BEFORE every skip branch, so both describe 'the scheduler considered this job' rather than 'this job ran'. Measured: run_count 9 for 4 real firings. Move the increment below the skip branches so only a firing that reaches a queued entry counts. JobRun rows already carry an honest status and must not change. (F13) hub/hub/api/v1/jobs.py: PATCH {enabled:true} on a loop whose ending_state is set returns 200 and leaves a contradictory state (enabled true, stopped_at set, ending_state 'completed'), then the next firing re-stops it a minute later and the operator's action is silently undone. Refuse it with a message saying what to do instead: give the loop work, or create a new one. (F1, backend half) hub/hub/scheduler.py: refuse a cron expression that restricts BOTH day-of-month and day-of-week, at job creation and update, naming the ambiguity and suggesting two jobs. Measured: '0 0 15 * 5' is stored with next_run 2026-08-28 and actually fires 2027-05-15, because APScheduler's CronTrigger ANDs the two fields while croniter ORs them. Note hub/ui/src/lib/cron.ts's describeCron already declines this shape in prose.

queue.title: Dashboard truth: all UI source changes, no bundle rebuild yet
queue.detail: Make every change under hub/ui/src in this one item so the committed bundle is rebuilt exactly once, in Q4. (F17) The rail reads agent.last_seen at AgentTree.tsx:163-167, and last_seen is populated ONLY from a heartbeat row (api/v1/agents.py:537), which only a self-registered agent posts. So every Hub-managed agent reads 'No activity yet' forever, including one that just did nine runs. Derive it from the agent's most recent run or output instead; no migration, the data exists in runs.started_at and agent_outputs.timestamp. (F19) TaskCard.tsx renders neither prerequisites nor dependents, though GET /tasks already returns a populated prerequisites array carrying each prerequisite's status, so a gated task looks like any ordinary pending card. Mark it. (F9) Add an inline note, NOT a dialog, on the approve control stating which commit will be merged into which branch: approving runs task_integration and cherry-picks the accepted evidence's commit into the main branch, which is a write the operator is not currently warned about. (F14) A task whose run is blocked on an unanswered ask_user still reads in_progress with blocked_reason null, because block_task_for_question is called only from run_divergence.evaluate_run_end. Surface 'waiting on you' on the card without changing the status. (F2) JobForm.tsx:193 and JobsPage.tsx:182 both say 'server time'; the scheduler is pinned to UTC (scheduler.py:626 and :683) and cron.ts computes in UTC deliberately. Change the word to UTC. On this machine local time is UTC+1 today, so the label is wrong by an hour. (F1, UI half) Align cron.ts and the JobCard/JobForm previews with whatever the Q2 refusal leaves legal, so the card and the form can no longer give two different next-run answers.

queue.title: Bundle, full verification, and the morning summary
queue.detail: cd hub/ui && npm run build, then from the repo root py -3.11 scripts/refresh_ui_bundle.py. IMPORTANT: git's CRLF normalisation on commit invalidates the stamp, so commit first and then rebuild and re-stamp AFTER that commit, or /health reports ui_stale on a clean tree. This cost the previous session a cycle. Then run: py -3.11 -m pytest hub/tests/ -q (expect 2758+ passed, 84 skipped, 1 xpassed, about 9 minutes); cd hub/ui && npx vitest run; uvx ruff@0.15.22 check src/ hub/ tests/; uvx black@26.5.1 --check src/ hub/hub/ hub/tests/ tests/; npx openspec validate --changes --strict. Read the full diff for accidental legacy revival, generated debris and unrelated files. Then write the morning summary at the log_file path: what landed per finding id, what did not and why, and anything that surprised you.

F4 is fixed only for the two branch names the Hub already knew: detect_main_branch walks MAIN_BRANCH_NAMES, which is exactly ('main', 'master'). A project on 'develop' or 'trunk' still opens with main_branch null and still needs you to set it in settings. Widening what the Hub recognises is a separate decision and was deliberately not taken unattended -- guessing that the single branch of a one-branch repository is its trunk is plausible, but it is a guess that ends in a cherry-pick into that branch.
